sections.heading: What a Repair Call Usually Turns Up
body: Most repair calls come down to a short list of causes. Here is what the signs usually mean, and what we do about each.

items.title: A breaker that keeps tripping
items.text: An overloaded circuit, a short or a ground fault. One that trips again right after you reset it is telling you something, so we find out what.

items.title: A warm outlet or switch plate
items.text: A loose connection heats up. We open it, fix the connection and check the others on the same circuit.

items.title: Lights that flicker
items.text: One fixture is often the bulb or the fixture. Flicker in several rooms points to a loose connection or an overloaded service.

items.title: Part of the house is dead
items.text: A tripped breaker, a failed connection or storm damage. We trace it and tell you where it stopped.

sections.heading: Panel Upgrades and Breaker Boxes
body: An old panel, a breaker box with no room left, or a house that has added a new appliance can outgrow what's on the wall. We upgrade and relocate panels.
A panel change usually means a city permit, an inspection and the power company disconnecting service for part of the day. We walk you through each step before we begin.

sections.heading: What Usually Goes Wrong
body: Most repair calls come down to a short list of causes. Here is what the signs usually mean.

items.title: A breaker that keeps tripping
items.text: An overloaded circuit, a short or a ground fault. A breaker that trips again right after you reset it is telling you something, so don't keep flipping it back on.

items.title: An outlet or switch plate that's warm
items.text: A loose connection heats up. A warm or discolored plate, a burning smell or a buzz is worth a call the same day.

items.title: Outlets that stopped working
items.text: Often a tripped GFCI outlet somewhere else on the circuit, or a loose or failed connection. We check both.

items.title: Lights that flicker
items.text: One fixture is often the bulb or the fixture itself. Flicker across several rooms, or when a big appliance starts, points to a loose connection or an overloaded service.

items.title: Part of the house is dead
items.text: A tripped breaker, a failed connection or storm damage. If the meter box or the line from the pole is damaged, the utility has to be part of the fix.

items.title: Old wiring or earlier DIY work
items.text: Older homes and earlier DIY work hide surprises. We show you what we find and what your options are.

sections.quote: I've had Julian from ElectriCraft out several times since starting the restoration of my 1910 Bungalow. He has done nothing but excellent work and knows a lot of the how they "used to do things" back in the day.
sections.name: Danny L.

sections.heading: A Repair, or Something Bigger?
body: A lot of repairs are small: a worn outlet, a loose connection, a bad switch. We fix those and say so.

Sometimes a repair points to something bigger, like an overloaded circuit or an old panel. When it does, you hear it straight, with your options and what each involves. Doing a bigger job in steps is one of them.

sections.heading: Older Homes
body: Houses built decades ago have often been added to over the years. You can find outlets with no ground, boxes that were never meant for today's loads and wiring from several different eras.
Tell us how old your house is when you call, and what you know has been changed. It helps us come ready.

sections.heading: Before You Call
body: If you can do it safely, note which outlets or rooms are affected, when it started and what was running. Check whether a breaker has tripped, and look for a GFCI outlet that needs resetting.
Don't open the panel cover or touch anything that's scorched, wet or buzzing. If you see smoke or sparks, or smell burning, get everyone out and call 911.

items.q: How soon can someone come out?
items.a: It depends on the day's schedule. Our office hours are Monday to Friday, 7 AM to 5 PM. Call and we'll tell you when a technician can get there.

items.q: Will you tell me if it needs a bigger job?
items.a: Yes. We fix what you called about, tell you what else we see, and you decide what happens next.

items.q: What if the problem comes and goes?
items.a: Tell us when it happens and what's running at the time. A problem that comes and goes is harder to catch, and we'd rather see it happen than guess.

items.q: Do you work on older homes?
items.a: Yes. Tell us how old the house is and what you know about earlier work, and we'll plan around it.

items.q: Do you work on commercial buildings?
items.a: Yes. We also do commercial electrical installation and industrial electrical repairs.

items.q: Is the repair covered by a warranty?
items.a: Our residential electrical services carry a one-year warranty. Ask us what it covers when you call.

sections.heading: What Goes Into a Lighting Job
body: A light looks simple once it's up. Getting there takes a few decisions, and we make them with you.

items.title: Where the wiring runs
items.text: A new light needs power and a switch to control it. In a finished ceiling or wall, we plan the route before we cut anything.

items.title: Recessed lights
items.text: They need room above the ceiling and have to be rated for the spot. We check what's up there first.

items.title: Ceiling fans
items.text: A fan needs a box rated to hold its weight and its motion, not just a light. We check that the box you have can take it.

items.title: Vaulted ceilings
items.text: These are harder to reach and plan. Tell us the ceiling height when you call so we arrive ready.

items.title: Dimmers
items.text: Not every dimmer works with every bulb, and a mismatch causes buzzing or flicker. We match the dimmer to your fixtures.

items.title: Damp and outdoor spots
items.text: Lights outside, in a bathroom or over a tub need fixtures and wiring rated for damp or wet locations. Tell us where you want them.

sections.quote: We had Jimmy and Ben install 4 more wafer lights in our basement, a light under the stairs in storage area and install a GFCI on the wet bar. They were very professional and did a great job. They worked very fast and cleaned up the mess too.
sections.name: Robert B.

sections.heading: Ceiling Fans
body: A ceiling fan is a light that moves, and the box it hangs from matters. A fan pulls and swings on its mount every day, so the box has to be rated to carry it.
We check the box, the wiring and the switch. If you want the fan and the light on separate controls, tell us. That can mean an extra wire run, and we'll say so up front.

sections.heading: Switches and Dimmers
body: A new light is a good moment to look at the switches. Three-way switches, dimmers and separate controls for a fan and a light all change what has to be run behind the wall.
Tell us how you'd like to control each light. We'll tell you what that takes, and show you the simpler way if there is one.

sections.heading: Light That Looks Right
body: Lighting is easy to get wrong. Too few lights leave dark corners, and one switch for a whole room means it's all or nothing.
Tell us how you use the room. We'll talk through where lights, switches and dimmers could go, and you pick what suits the space and your budget.

sections.heading: Fixing or Replacing an Old Fixture
body: If a fixture flickers, hums or has a cracked socket, it isn't always the bulb. We check the fixture and the wiring behind it.
Some fixtures are worth keeping and rebuilding, and some are worth replacing. We tell you which we think it is, and you decide.

sections.heading: Before You Call
body: Note the ceiling height and what kind of ceiling you have, finished or open to an attic. Tell us what you want installed and whether you already have the fixtures.
If a fixture is sparking, smoking or smells like burning, turn off its breaker if you can do it safely, and call us.

items.a: Yes. We check that the box in your ceiling can carry a fan, and replace it if it can't.

items.q: Can you add a light where there isn't one now?
items.a: Often, yes. It depends on what's behind the walls and ceiling. We look and give you your options.

items.q: Can you put in a dimmer?
items.a: Yes. We match the dimmer to your bulbs and fixtures so it doesn't buzz or flicker.

items.q: Do you clean up when you're done?
items.a: Yes. We leave the room tidy.

items.q: What if the wiring needs more than lighting work?
items.a: We tell you what we see and what it means. You decide whether to do it now, later or in steps.

footer.about: ElectriCraft is a Wichita electrical company serving homes, commercial buildings and industrial sites. We repair, install and upgrade, and we explain what we find in plain words.
why: We explain what we find in plain words
We clean up after the job

Your site is laid out at desktop width, so on a phone a visitor scrolls sideways to read it, and your homepage has an empty main headline. Someone standing at a warm outlet with a phone in hand has a hard time seeing what you do.

Your reviews describe an electrician who tells people what else they found: wiring that needed protecting, something an inspector missed, what to know about an older house. Today those words sit on Google, not on your site.
So the demo tells one story on every page. It opens with Electrician in Wichita, KS, and gives electrical repair and lighting installation a page each, because your site has no page for either.

lead.heading: Why we led with finding what else is wrong
lead.text: The scariest moment for a Wichita homeowner is a warm outlet or a panel they don't trust, and right behind it is not knowing whether the electrician is selling something. Fixing the problem, then telling you plainly what else we see, answers both. We checked the Wichita competitors' sites we could open, and none of them states it.
